quests.instruction: A glass jar breaks in the classroom, and a classmate is about to walk toward the pieces. What is the best order of actions?
quests.correctAnswer: Warn them, tell the teacher, then stay back 🛑
options: Warn them, tell the teacher, then stay back 🛑
Pick up the pieces yourself, then tell no one 🧤
Finish your work, then mention it later ✏️
quests.explanation: Warning your classmate prevents an injury, and the teacher can clean up broken glass safely.
quests.funFact: Broken glass should be cleaned up by an adult with a brush and dustpan.

quests.instruction: Your group wants to display a poster on the notice board for a week. What should you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask which pins or putty are allowed 📌
options: Use plenty of tape across all edges 📼
Ask which pins or putty are allowed 📌
Staple the corners straight into the wall 🗜️
quests.explanation: Asking first protects the board and the wall, and shows respect for shared spaces.
quests.funFact: Reusable putty is gentle on walls.

quests.instruction: Lunch is in three minutes, and your paintbrush is still wet. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Rinse the brush, put it away, then line up 🖌️
options: Take it with you to the cafeteria 🍽️
Rinse the brush, put it away, then line up 🖌️
Leave it in the paint to soak overnight 🎨
quests.hint: Care for tools before you leave.
quests.explanation: Rinsing and storing the brush keeps it in good shape and the room tidy before you go.
quests.funFact: A brush left in paint can bend its bristles permanently.

quests.instruction: You need reliable facts about the Moon for homework due tomorrow. Where is the best place to look?
quests.correctAnswer: A non-fiction library book 📚
options: A comic book about space heroes 🦸
A non-fiction library book 📚
A story an older student told you 🗣️
quests.hint: Choose a source written by experts.
quests.explanation: Non-fiction library books are written and checked by people who know the topic.
quests.funFact: School libraries often have a reference section with atlases and encyclopedias.

quests.instruction: You find five books on the Moon, but you can only take two home. Which choice is best?
quests.correctAnswer: The two that best answer your questions 📚
options: The two thickest books on the shelf ⚖️
The two with the nicest covers 🖼️
The two that best answer your questions 📚
quests.explanation: Choosing the books that match your questions makes your research efficient.
quests.funFact: Skimming contents pages helps you decide quickly.

quests.instruction: A book's index says 'craters 12, 14'. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Turn to pages 12 and 14 🔖
options: Look only at page 2 ☝️
Skip them both 🙈
Turn to pages 12 and 14 🔖
quests.hint: Numbers show where the topic is.
quests.explanation: Indexes list topics with page numbers, so you can go straight to what you need.
quests.funFact: Indexes list topics in alphabetical order.

quests.instruction: Your school has a nut-free table for a classmate with a nut allergy, and you brought a peanut butter sandwich. What is the responsible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat at another table and wash your hands 🧼
options: Sit beside your classmate and keep it covered 🥜
Eat at another table and wash your hands 🧼
Offer your classmate a small bite 🤝
quests.explanation: Sitting at a different table and washing up keeps traces of nuts away from someone who could be seriously ill.
quests.funFact: Even a tiny trace of an allergen can cause a reaction for some people.

quests.instruction: After tasting a new food, your lips feel itchy and puffy. What should you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a teacher right away 🚨
options: Tell a teacher right away 🚨
Wait to see if it passes ⏳
Drink water and keep eating 🥤
quests.hint: An allergic reaction needs adult help.
quests.explanation: Itching and swelling can be signs of an allergic reaction, so adults must know immediately.
quests.funFact: Allergic reactions can start within minutes.

quests.instruction: You've finished eating, and there are 10 minutes of lunch left. What is the responsible thing to do before playing?
quests.correctAnswer: Clear your tray and wash your hands 🧼
options: Hurry out to the playground first 🏃
Leave your tray for the staff to clear 🍽️
Clear your tray and wash your hands 🧼
quests.explanation: Clearing your tray and washing your hands is part of leaving the eating area ready for others.
quests.funFact: Responsible habits keep shared places pleasant.

quests.instruction: Your group has three tasks (research, drawing, writing) and three members. What is a fair plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Each person picks a task and you check in 🤝
options: The oldest student picks tasks for everyone 👑
Each person picks a task and you check in 🤝
One person does all three tasks alone 🦸
quests.explanation: Dividing tasks means all members contribute, and check-ins keep the group working together.
quests.funFact: Group projects work best when all members have a role.

quests.instruction: One teammate's part is not finished and the deadline is near. What is a helpful response?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask what help they need and offer yours 🤝
options: Tell everyone the work is late 📣
Take over their part without asking ✂️
Ask what help they need and offer yours 🤝
quests.explanation: Offering help and working together gets the project finished and keeps the group friendly.
quests.funFact: Teams often finish faster when they help each other.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says each person must speak in the presentation, but you feel shy. What could help?
quests.correctAnswer: Practice your part with a partner first 🗣️
options: Practice your part with a partner first 🗣️
Skip your part and let others speak 🙈
Speak very quietly so nobody hears 🤫
quests.explanation: Practicing with a partner builds confidence and helps you remember your part.
quests.funFact: Actors rehearse many times before a performance.

quests.instruction: A classmate is climbing on a table to reach a high shelf. What is the best response?
quests.correctAnswer: Calmly ask them to stop, get an adult 🙋
options: Cheer them on from the floor below 📣
Calmly ask them to stop, get an adult 🙋
Hold the table so it doesn't move 🪑
quests.hint: Care about safety without making a scene.
quests.explanation: A calm request and an offer to get an adult prevent a fall and keep things friendly.
quests.funFact: Tables and chairs are not made for standing on.

quests.instruction: In science, your partner reaches for a beaker of unknown liquid. What do you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Wait, let's ask our teacher first.' 🧪
options: 'Smell it closely to find out what it is.' 👃
'Go ahead, it looks like plain water.' 👍
'Wait, let's ask our teacher first.' 🧪
quests.explanation: Checking with the teacher first avoids harm from unknown substances.
quests.funFact: Labels on containers tell what's inside.

quests.instruction: A friend is upset and crying in the washroom and asks you not to tell anyone. What is a good choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay kind and tell a trusted adult 💙
options: Promise to say nothing and walk away 🤐
Stay kind and tell a trusted adult 💙
Tell the whole class so they can help 📢
quests.explanation: Telling a trusted adult gets your friend help, even when it is hard.
quests.funFact: Good friends sometimes ask adults to help.

quests.instruction: Your timetable says Computer Lab (Room C3) at 11:00. It's 10:55 in Room A1. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack up and head to Room C3 now 💻
options: Wait for the bell to ring twice 🔔
Pack up and head to Room C3 now 💻
Stay in Room A1 until someone comes 🪑
quests.explanation: Leaving a few minutes early gives you time to find the room and arrive on time.
quests.funFact: Moving between rooms is quicker if you know the way.

quests.instruction: Your lesson was moved from Room 5 to Hall B, but you aren't sure. How can you confirm?
quests.correctAnswer: Check the notice board or ask 🙋
options: Guess and head to Hall B anyway 🤷
Stay in Room 5 and wait alone 🪑
Check the notice board or ask 🙋
quests.explanation: Notice boards and teachers give accurate information about changes.
quests.funFact: Schools post room changes on notice boards or in announcements.

quests.instruction: You arrive at the library for your lesson, and it's crowded with another class. What is a good choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask the librarian where to wait 🙋
options: Ask the librarian where to wait 🙋
Push to the front to find a seat 🏃
Leave and spend the lesson outside 🛝
quests.explanation: Asking staff gives clear directions, so you don't create confusion.
quests.funFact: Libraries can only fit a certain number of people comfortably.

quests.instruction: Your science notes are on loose pages, and your teacher wants them neat and in order. What is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Number the pages and keep them in a folder 📁
options: Number the pages and keep them in a folder 📁
Stack them loosely at the bottom of your bag 🎒
Fold them small to fit in your pencil case 📄
quests.explanation: Page numbers and a folder keep notes in order, so you can find information quickly.
quests.funFact: Dates and page numbers make revision easier.

quests.instruction: Your teacher wants a neat, labeled diagram of a flower. Which set of tools is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Sharp pencil, ruler, eraser ✏️
options: Sharp pencil, ruler, eraser ✏️
Thick marker, glue, scissors 🖊️
Paint, sponge, crayon 🎨
quests.explanation: A sharp pencil and ruler give neat lines, and an eraser fixes errors.
quests.funFact: Scientists draw clear diagrams to show how things work.

quests.instruction: In a plant diagram, which part takes in water from the soil?
quests.correctAnswer: Root 🌱
options: Leaf 🍃
Flower 🌸
Root 🌱
quests.explanation: Roots take in water and nutrients from the soil and hold the plant in place.
quests.funFact: Some roots can grow deeper than the plant is tall.

quests.instruction: You find a classmate's eraser in your bag at home. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Return it tomorrow and say sorry 🙏
options: Keep it because it's so small 🧽
Return it tomorrow and say sorry 🙏
Leave it at home and say nothing 🏠
quests.hint: Fix it as soon as you can.
quests.explanation: Returning it with an apology shows honesty and care for others' things.
quests.funFact: Small accidents are forgiven more quickly when you are honest.

quests.instruction: You notice your teacher gave you two marks too many on your test. What is the honest choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Politely tell your teacher 🙋
options: Politely tell your teacher 🙋
Say nothing and enjoy it 🤫
Show your friends 📣
quests.hint: Honesty counts even when it costs you.
quests.explanation: Telling the teacher corrects the mistake and shows you value honesty.
quests.funFact: Honest people are trusted by others.

quests.instruction: You promised to bring a game for the class and forgot. What is a good response?
quests.correctAnswer: Say sorry and bring it the next day 🙂
options: Say it was never really your job 🙈
Say a classmate forgot to remind you 👈
Say sorry and bring it the next day 🙂
quests.hint: Keep promises or make them right.
quests.explanation: Apologizing and following through shows responsibility.
quests.funFact: A promise is a commitment to others.

quests.instruction: During a fire drill, the usual exit is blocked by a pile of chairs. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher and follow another route 🚪
options: Go back to your desk and wait there 🪑
Climb over the chairs to reach the door 🪑
Tell your teacher and follow another route 🚪
quests.explanation: Teachers choose another safe route, so students don't get hurt by climbing.
quests.funFact: Pathways must always be clear of obstacles.

quests.instruction: During the drill, a classmate with a sprained ankle is moving slowly. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the teacher so they can help 🙋
options: Tell the teacher so they can help 🙋
Pull them by the arm to hurry them 💪
Rush ahead and leave them behind 🏃
quests.hint: Don't try to fix it alone.
quests.explanation: The teacher can arrange safe help for someone who is hurt.
quests.funFact: Schools plan for students who need extra help in drills.

quests.instruction: After a drill, you notice a classmate isn't in your line. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher straight away ☝️
options: Go and look yourself 🏃
Wait to see if they show up ⏳
Tell your teacher straight away ☝️
quests.explanation: Reporting right away lets the teacher check and find them quickly.
quests.funFact: Teachers call out names after a drill to be sure everyone is there.

quests.instruction: You need to submit work on a school computer, but the internet isn't working. What is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher or computer teacher 🙋
options: Tell your teacher or computer teacher 🙋
Keep clicking the same button harder 🖱️
Unplug the computer and plug it back in 🔌
quests.explanation: Staff can check the connection or give another way to submit.
quests.funFact: Many problems are solved by restarting the network, which only staff should do.

quests.instruction: A website says to download a free game to finish your project. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Don't download it; ask your teacher 🚫
options: Don't download it; ask your teacher 🚫
Download it right away to save time ⬇️
Ask a friend to download it for you 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
quests.explanation: Unknown downloads can hide harmful programs, so ask an adult.
quests.funFact: Never download files from sites you don't know.

quests.instruction: You typed half a story, and the computer froze. What is a good habit for next time?
quests.correctAnswer: Save your work often 💾
options: Type faster ⚡
Save your work often 💾
Never use computers 🚫
quests.explanation: Saving often means you lose very little if something goes wrong.
quests.funFact: Many programs also save automatically.
